Recording the description model now.

message.reasoning_content: The contract requires order-4 joint uniformity, but the initial probe only checks marginals and pairs. The kernel's fold: seed & mask, then parity fold. seed & mask gives up to 1024 values; parity of (seed & mask) after XOR folding = parity of seed & mask. So keep = parity(seed & mask_j) ^ offset_j. For 4 channels: bits of seed restricted to masks. Since masks are 10-bit values from 1..1023 chosen without replacement, parity function is a linear functional over GF(2) of seed bits (10 bits). Masks distinct → distinct nonzero linear functionals → independent parities → order-4 (indeed full 8-channel) uniformity. Actually parity of seed&mask is GF(2) linear in seed bits, and masks with distinct bit-patterns give independent linear forms; 8 distinct masks chosen from 1..1023 are distinct, so independent. So the kernel likely satisfies the contract. But risk: masks could be equal? replace=False ensures distinct. Offsets just flip. Also seeds are 0..1023, so 10 bits exactly; linear forms of rank 8 → each pattern appears exactly 2^(10-8)=4 times... wait rank 8 among 1024 seeds gives 2^2=4 seeds per pattern → counts/1024 = 4/1024 = 1/256, not 1/16. For 4 channels, rank 4 forms → 2^6=64 seeds per pattern → 64/1024=1/16 exactly. Good. Risk: masks could differ only in bits beyond seed's 10 bits — no, masks < 1024, 10 bits. Distinct masks → independent parities. So contract holds exactly. But Skeptic should verify rank ≥8 of masks — that's evidence. Record description update.
